questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

```yaml
kind: ClusterPolicy
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-resources-readonly
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
  - name: enforce-tls-secret-mount
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "TLS secret must be mounted at /etc/tls from Secret tls-cert-<app>"
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - secret:
              secretName: tls-cert-?*
              items:
              - key: tls.crt
                path: etc/tls/tls.crt
```

## Sample Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-cert-payment-service
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: payment-service:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tls-cert-payment-service
```

## Sample Non-Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: insecure-service:latest
        # Missing: resources.limits/requests
        # Missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem
        # Missing: TLS secret mount
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

Why This Is Asked

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical data validation in CI/CD with a concrete schema and gating.

## Key Concepts
- CSV header validation
- Type coercion and data quality
- CI gate integration (GitHub Actions)

## Code Example
```python
import csv, sys
from datetime import datetime

EXPECTED = {
  'id': int,
  'date': 'date',
  'amount': float,
  'category': str
}

DATE_FMT = '%Y-%m-%d'

def parse_row(row):
  row['id'] = int(row['id'])
  row['date'] = datetime.strptime(row['date'], DATE_FMT).date()
  row['amount'] = float(row['amount'])
  row['category'] = str(row['category'])
  return row

def main(path):
  with open(path, newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    header = set(reader.fieldnames or [])
    if header != set(EXPECTED.keys()):
      print('Header mismatch:', reader.fieldnames)
      sys.exit(1)
    for r in reader:
      try:
        parse_row(r)
      except Exception as e:
        print('Type/Parse error', e, r)
        sys.exit(1)
  print('OK')

if __name__ == '__main__':
  sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```

- How would you adapt for evolving schemas without breaking the pipeline?
- How would you test locally with representative failing/passing CSVs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to express policy-as-code for security/compliance in multi-cloud clusters, combining network isolation, identity controls, and outbound security.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- NetworkPolicy as runtime guard
- Pod securityContext and automountServiceAccountToken control
- mTLS and central CA validation for outbound traffic
- CI verification using kubectl, gatekeeper audits

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"
        not has_ns_deny_ingress(input)
        msg := "Deployment namespace must have a deny-ingress NetworkPolicy and allow only whitelisted sources."
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no deny ingress and automount enabled)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (deny ingress, trusted SA, automount disabled)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal NetworkPolicy (deny ingress by default, allow from trusted namespace)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

## CI Verification Steps
- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
- kubectl apply -f passing.yaml should succeed and Gatekeeper should record no violations.
- Validate that namespaces have the required NetworkPolicy objects and that deployments use trusted SAs with automountServiceAccountToken disabled.
